clue.text: Falls not always forecast?

parts.note: a weather presenter's phrase for showers that come only now and then, read as a description of intermittent falls

explanation.surface: A question about whether waterfalls, or tumbles, can be predicted.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecast of intermittent showers predicts precipitation that falls only some of the time.

clue.text: Transport edition

explanation.surface: A transport publication.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is the full form of bus, and also a volume collecting several works.

clue.text: Doing well but proceeding to get a lengthy penalty

definitions.text: proceeding to get a lengthy penalty

explanation.surface: Someone thriving despite heading for a big punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means progressing nicely; split, it reads as arriving with a long monetary charge.

clue.text: Little Alexandra loses a part of the waistband

indicators.note: loses means a letter is taken away from the pet name

parts.note: Sasha is a familiar short form of Alexandra

explanation.surface: Young Alexandra drops a piece of her belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a broad band of cloth worn around the middle.

clue.text: Boy's terrific portion of seafood

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A boy enjoys a great serving of shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is a shellfish eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: A right boater removed from the tree gardens

indicators.note: removed is read as re-moved, moved around again, so the hat's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A straw hat is taken out of the botanical garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' reads as taken away but signals the letters of BOATER moved about.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreta, plural of arboretum, are collections of trees grown for study and display.

clue.text: Recorded another form of delivery

explanation.surface: A note that a different postal service was used.
explanation.definitionFit: It means entered in an official list, and is also a postal service with signed receipt, an alternative to recorded mail.

clue.text: Written down but not in colourful language presumably

explanation.surface: Something is set out in writing, though not in vivid prose.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in print; black ink on paper is literally without colour.

clue.text: Alone he does not succeed

parts.note: succeed in the sense of inherit: a person sharing an inheritance with others

explanation.surface: A gloomy remark that a man fails on his own.
explanation.definitionFit: A coheir is one of several joint inheritors, so never takes the estate by himself.

clue.text: Meissen shattered — that's retribution

indicators.note: shattered porcelain is in pieces, so the letters of the china name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Breaking precious Meissen china brings punishment on the culprit.
explanation.walkthrough: Meissen is a German porcelain maker; 'shattered' rearranges its seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of vengeance, and the word now means deserved punishment.

clue.text: Jacks rings after disease-germ had become a cause of anxiety

indicators.note: after places the sailors and rings behind the germ word

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for a germ causing illness
a jack tar is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the usual abbreviation
two O shapes look like rings

explanation.surface: Sailors become worried about an infection spreading on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacks' looks like playing cards or tools, but means sailors, AB for able-bodied seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugaboo is an imagined object of fear, a bogey that worries people.

clue.text: Where to deposit money by the river

explanation.surface: Advice on saving cash at a riverside spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A financial institution takes deposits, and the sloping ground beside a river shares the same name.

clue.text: Viola finds the seas are rough

indicators.note: rough seas are churned up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone named Viola, or a viola player, discovers the sea is choppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viola' reads as a name or instrument but is the plant genus that includes pansies.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartsease is the wild pansy, a plant in the genus Viola.

clue.text: Legally one can go no faster

definitions.text: Legally one can go no faster

parts.words: Legally one can go no faster
parts.note: the maximum rate of driving permitted by law on a road

explanation.surface: A statement that the law caps how fast you travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Road signs set a maximum permitted velocity for motorists.

clue.text: Smart agent has short sleep inside

indicators.note: inside puts the doze within the word for a secret agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a nap is a brief sleep

explanation.surface: A well-dressed secret agent dozes off briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy, like smart, can describe stylish dress or a quick, sharp manner.

clue.text: One running with indecent haste?

parts.note: indecent is taken literally: a person dashing about naked, as at a sports match

explanation.surface: A remark about someone rushing in an unseemly hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs naked through a public place is doing it in an indecent way and quickly.

clue.text: The way one had a restless desire to have it fastened

parts.note: ST, for street, is a way or road
someone who itched had a fidgety longing

explanation.surface: Somebody wanted it sewn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitched means sewn together, held with thread.

clue.text: A characteristic of houses perhaps

explanation.surface: A remark about a typical feature of homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A property is a quality or attribute, and also real estate such as buildings.

clue.text: Buccaneer renegade tucking into tart

indicators.note: tucking into means the traitor word goes inside the pastry word

parts.note: a tart is a kind of pie
a rat is a deserter or turncoat

explanation.surface: A traitorous sea robber eats a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' tempts you to picture someone eating the tart, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer is a sea robber of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Shed ale not spilt!

indicators.note: spilt beer is scattered, so these letters fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A plea not to waste any beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall.

clue.text: Not having a chance when it's not in Old French or Italian

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
OF is the abbreviation for Old French

explanation.surface: Something is hopeless when absent from two old languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of it means excluded from contention, with no hope of winning.

clue.text: Moving up and down endlessly on a spool

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the motion word is cut off

parts.note: bobbing means moving up and down

explanation.surface: Something bounces ceaselessly on a reel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobbin is a reel holding thread or yarn.

clue.text: Normal rule

explanation.surface: Ordinary rules apply.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means standard or official issue; as a noun it is a law or directive.

clue.text: Hard worker pulls back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for pulls from right to left

parts.note: tows means pulls along

explanation.surface: A diligent labourer drags something backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is someone who studies hard, a British word for a diligent student.

clue.text: As it happens it is charged with energy

explanation.surface: A broadcast is electrically charged.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast in real time is unrecorded; a wire carrying current is electrically energised.

clue.text: Right back and I give an expression of reserved doubt at the victory

indicators.note: back tells us to turn the short form of right round

parts.note: umph, a form of humph, is a grunt of scepticism

explanation.surface: Someone voices grudging scepticism at a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RT into TR; UMPH is a dictionary variant of humph.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great win or success.

clue.text: Sheriff's officer hit about to feel unwell

indicators.note: about means the word for strike goes around the word for being ill

parts.note: biff is informal for a punch or hit
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: A lawman's deputy, struck, is about to feel sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff carries out court orders for a sheriff, such as seizing goods.

clue.text: Financial stake in underwear business?

parts.note: a monetary share in a company, punningly read as concern with singlets, since a vest is an undergarment in British English

explanation.surface: Asking about money invested in a lingerie firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal stake gives someone reason to favour an outcome; the joke takes vested as wearing a singlet.
